mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase > 10,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the labor strength signal (p-value < 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% for three consecutive months indicates weakening demand for manufactured goods, which compresses earnings growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite the three-month INDPRO decline (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 233 (the most recent value at decision time) accompanied by a rise in residential housing starts (HOUST) suggests a soft landing, which supports risk-on sentiment and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 233 AND HOUST increases for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Moderate inflation cooling with improving housing market
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the interaction window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tighter labor market, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady but reducing future rate hike expectations, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE staying below 6.5% for the required period (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail sales (implied via a decline in PAYEMS of >15,000 jobs in a month) suggests consumer weakness, which dampens earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >15,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) during the trigger month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (implied by GDPC1 growth exceeding 2% for four consecutive quarters) forecasts stronger economic momentum, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 2% for four consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the sustained GDP growth signal (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below their respective 2023 Q4 averages for two months suggest supply-side easing, which reduces upward price pressure and supports risk-on positioning, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 98.95 AND CPIAUCSL < 233 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the interaction window.
